About HAWA

Two cities, three values, one Constitution.

ہمارا خواب
Our vision Draft wording, to be confirmed

A united, caring Hyderabadi Muslim community in Western Australia, rooted in Imaan, Khayr and Barakah, where no family starts over alone.

From the city of the Charminar to the city on the Swan

0 km

Many of us crossed the Indian Ocean alone or as young families. HAWA exists so nobody has to start over without a community around them.

Non-profit, non-political, non-sectarian. HAWA does not promote any ideology, maslak or school of thought, and must not unreasonably discriminate on gender, profession, age, disability or political affiliation. Its income and property go only to its objects, never to members. It is not a registered charity unless and until it becomes one.

From clause 6 of the Constitution, adopted by the members on 3 September 2026, in four groups.

Important notes: migration, finance, disclaimers

Migration: under the Migration Act 1958 only registered migration agents, Australian legal practitioners or exempt persons may give immigration assistance. HAWA volunteers will not assess visa options, fill in applications or recommend agents. Check any agent's MARN on the OMARA register.

Finance: providers described as offering sharia-compliant products have not been assessed by HAWA. Check licences on Moneysmart or the ASIC register.

Information only, not advice, and not an endorsement. Helpline hours shown in Perth time. Last checked October 2026.

New to WA

Your first 30 days in Western Australia, and the Indian services you will need from Perth.

0of 0 done

Tick items off as you go. Your ticks stay on this device only. Checked against official sources in October 2026; rules change, so follow the links before you act.

Week 1

First things

  1. Save the numbers that matter

    Emergency 000. Nurse advice 24/7: healthdirect 1800 022 222. Free interpreter in Urdu, Telugu or Hindi: TIS National 131 450.

    healthdirect ↗TIS National ↗
  2. Get a local SIM

    Carriers must check your ID before activating a prepaid SIM, so take your passport.

  3. Open a bank account

    Within 6 weeks of arrival your passport is the only ID you need. After that you need two forms of ID.

    Home Affairs ↗
  4. Apply for your Tax File Number

    Free and online if your visa has work rights. It arrives by post within 28 days, so don't apply twice. Never pay an agent for this.

    ATO ↗
  5. Create your myGov account

    You need an email address. Later you link Medicare, the ATO and Centrelink to it.

    myGov ↗
  6. Sort out driving early

    India is a non-recognised country in WA. Permanent residents can drive on an Indian licence for 3 months only, then need a WA licence: a verification letter from the Indian consulate (allow about 4 weeks), a theory test and a driving assessment. Temporary residents can keep driving on a current licence.

    Transport WA ↗

    Ask for the consulate letter in week 1. It is the slowest step. See India services.

  7. Temporary visa? Keep health cover in place

    Many temporary visas carry condition 8501, which requires adequate health insurance for the whole stay. Check your conditions in VEVO.

    Home Affairs ↗
Week 2

Health, home and school

  1. Enrol in Medicare

    You can enrol once you hold a permanent visa or have applied for one. India has no reciprocal health agreement with Australia, so temporary visa holders rely on private cover.

    Services Australia ↗
  2. Find a GP near you

    Use the healthdirect Service Finder, including after-hours GPs. Doctors can book a free interpreter for you.

    Service Finder ↗
  3. Enrol the children in school

    Kindergarten if your child turns 4 by 30 June, Pre-primary if 5. Most schools have a local intake area. Bring an immunisation statement from the last 2 months and visa evidence. Families on a 482 visa pay $4,000 a year per family (waivers apply).

    Department of Education ↗Temporary visa fees ↗
  4. Renting: protect your bond

    Bond is at most 4 weeks' rent. Your landlord must lodge it with Bonds Administration within 14 days, and you get a record from them. Free tenancy advice: Circle Green, 08 6148 3636.

    Consumer Protection WA ↗
  5. Get a SmartRider for Transperth

    Autoload saves 20% on fares. School students travel free on weekdays in term with a Student SmartRider.

    Transperth ↗
By day 30

Work, support and community

  1. Know the Centrelink waiting periods

    New residents wait 1 year for Family Tax Benefit Part A and 4 years for most payments such as JobSeeker. FTB Part B and Child Care Subsidy have no wait.

    Services Australia ↗
  2. Get free career help

    Jobs and Skills Centres help with resumes, training and job search: 13 64 64. The WA Overseas Qualifications Unit assesses your degree free of charge.

    Jobs and Skills WA ↗Qualifications Unit ↗
  3. Free English classes

    The Adult Migrant English Program is free, with free childcare during class. Register within 6 months of your visa start.

    AMEP ↗
  4. Free settlement support

    Settlement caseworkers help people who arrived in the last 5 years, with priority for family and humanitarian visas.

    Home Affairs ↗
  5. Find your community

    Find your nearest masjid on the Salah page, join HAWA free, and ask for a free airport pickup or a welcome call.

    Salah and masjidsJoin HAWAAirport pickup
Changed in 2026. Indian consular services in Australia paused for three weeks in July 2026 and restarted on 23 July through VFS Global. A new tender may change the provider again, so check cgiperth.gov.in before you go.

Where you apply: VFS Global centre

Passports, OCI, visas, police certificates and attestation are lodged here, not at the consulate.

Book an appointment ↗

Renew your Indian passport

Apply on the Global Passport Seva Portal, then lodge at VFS in person or by post. You need an Indian address for police verification. Allow about 4 weeks if your passport was issued in Australia, about 8 weeks if issued in India.

Passport Seva (GPSP) ↗VFS checklists ↗

OCI card

Apply online, then lodge in person at VFS with originals (no postal OCI since 1 April 2026). Re-issue is needed only once, for the first new passport after you turn 20. Other new passports are uploaded free online within 3 months.

ociservices.gov.in ↗

Visiting India on an Australian passport

Use the official e-Visa site only, at least 4 days before travel. Look-alike agent sites charge extra.

Indian e-Visa (official) ↗

Police Clearance Certificate

Apply on the Passport Seva portal and lodge with your passport, visa copy and photos at VFS. Processing time varies.

VFS checklist ↗

Sending documents home

A Power of Attorney or property paper for India: sign before a JP or notary, then have it attested at VFS. Documents issued in Australia can instead carry a DFAT apostille. Ask the bank or registrar in India which they accept.

Attestation ↗DFAT apostille ↗

Life certificate for pensioners

Sign in person before a consular officer (free), post a JP-attested form, or use Jeevan Pramaan online with Aadhaar.

Jeevan Pramaan ↗

Baby born in Australia

Register the birth with the consulate before or with the child's first Indian passport (Forms I and K, signed by both parents).

VFS checklist ↗

Becoming an Australian citizen

You must surrender your Indian passport straight away and get a surrender certificate. Travelling on it after citizenship attracts penalties.

Surrender checklist ↗

Driving licence verification letter

Needed to convert your Indian licence to a WA licence. Request it through VFS as soon as you arrive; it can take about 4 weeks.

Transport WA ↗

Information only, checked October 2026. HAWA is not a visa or passport agent and does not lodge applications. Fees change often; confirm on the official sites.

Join HAWA, free

Open to any Muslim who supports HAWA's objects (clause 9).

Preview: this form isn't connected yet. At launch it goes to the Secretary or Membership Officer.

Free

There is no membership fee. Under clause 14, when HAWA runs an activity, its costs are shared fairly among those who take part, as the committee decides.

Ordinary member

18 and over

  • Attend and speak at general meetings
  • One vote at general meetings
  • Stand for election to the committee
  • Receive notices, minutes and communications
  • Inspect HAWA's records as the Constitution allows

Associate member

Under 18, or friends of the community

  • Take part in all activities and events
  • Attend and speak at general meetings
  • No vote, and cannot hold committee office

For example, someone without a direct connection to Hyderabad or Telangana, or a young person under 18 (clause 11).

How to join

  1. ApplyYour name, contact details, the category you want, and your agreement to be bound by the Constitution. No nominator needed.
  2. Committee decisionConsidered as soon as practicable. An application can only be declined on reasonable grounds, with written reasons on request.
  3. WelcomeYou receive the Constitution, your confirmation and the WhatsApp Community invite.

As a member you agree to follow the Constitution and Code of Conduct, act honestly and in good faith, and treat everyone with courtesy and respect (clause 16).

Governance

Incorporated under the Associations Incorporation Act 2015 (WA). The founding committee serves until the first AGM.

The Constitution sets a committee of seven to nine: the four office bearers plus three to five ordinary committee members (clause 23). Assistant roles such as Joint Secretary carry no extra vote (clause 25).

If something goes wrong: the four-step path

Talk firstTry to resolve it directly within 14 days.
Written complaintLodge it with the Secretary. The other side gets to respond.
MediationAn independent mediator, if both sides agree. Costs shared.
DecisionBy the committee, or a general meeting if the committee is involved, with written reasons.

Clause 71, with natural justice under clause 72. Members keep the right to apply to the State Administrative Tribunal.

ConstitutionAdopted 3 Sep 2026. Published once registered by the Commissioner.
Code of ConductClause 70 sets the standard. A detailed policy may follow.
PrivacyClause 74: personal information used only for HAWA's purposes.
Child safety statementTo be drafted.
AGM papers and minutesMembers area.
Annual reportAfter the year ending 30 June 2027.
RegistrationIA number and ABN to be added.
FundingMembers' own contributions, donations, sponsorship and grants (clause 7c).

    Home/Questions
    سوالات

    Questions

    Asked at every gathering.

    Is there a membership fee?

    No. The Constitution sets no membership fee (clause 14). When HAWA runs an activity, the costs are shared fairly among those who take part, as the committee decides.

    Who can join?

    Any Muslim who supports HAWA's objects. Ordinary members are 18 or over and can vote and stand for the committee. Associate membership is for under-18s and friends of the community who want to take part without voting.

    Is HAWA linked to any political or religious group?

    No. HAWA is non-profit, non-political and non-sectarian. It does not promote any ideology, maslak or school of thought.

    How is the committee chosen?

    At each AGM, members elect the President, Vice-President, Secretary and Treasurer, plus three to five ordinary committee members, for one year. Nominations go to the Secretary at least 14 days before the AGM. If nominations exceed places, there is a ballot, secret if any member asks.

    How is HAWA's money handled?

    Through HAWA's own bank account, never personal accounts. Three office bearers are authorised signatories and any two must approve each payment. HAWA reports as a Tier 1 association, presents financial statements at each AGM, and members may inspect the financial records on reasonable notice.

    Can HAWA help with a funeral or repatriation?

    Yes. Supporting families with repatriation, funeral arrangements and burial is one of HAWA's objects, including coordination with the UAIA Burial Society. Use "I need help" and the welfare lead will call.

    How do I raise a concern?

    Talk to the person first, within 14 days. If that doesn't work, lodge a written complaint with the Secretary. Mediation can follow if both sides agree, then a committee decision with written reasons.
